correctness.rationale: Exact three-sample plurality enumeration gives F_i=z_i(1+z_i-S); the shared quadratic fixed-point equation forces at most two received-frequency values, parametrized exhaustively by multiplicity and ratio. Symmetric positive definite Jacobian gives exact tangent eigenvalues, and invariant-line cubic settles both nonhyperbolic boundaries. The convex-gradient potential gives L(F(x))-L(x)>=||F(x)-x||^2/2; finitely many fixed points and asymptotic regularity then prove convergence of every orbit. Verified with 24 exact three-message enumerations, 210 rational fixed-point/Jacobian cases, 4 symbolic gradient identities, 40 exact Lyapunov comparisons and the rational 3-state witness. No finite experiment is treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The motivating binary noisy three-majority paper asks whether 1/3 persists with arbitrary many opinions. The natural full-k answer has two distinct exact thresholds and an open interval with k+1 attracting equilibria, and the theorem proves global convergence for all deterministic population compositions. This is a substantive nonlinear coexistence boundary and complete fixed-point classification, not a small numerical increment or renamed known q-voter result; the explicit rational 3-opinion witness supplies a transparent benchmark.
